analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/provider/cli-reference.md: a date bump at line 3 and a new `Traffic:` bullet in the `darkbloom status` section (head lines 998-1009). It describes a local status line showing whether the coordinator can route work to the connection (eligible via App Attest lease or legacy verification, or the reason it is not), with a fix hint. It is sourced from ServingReadiness.swift and StatusCommand+Traffic.swift, neither of which is supplied here. The doc says the line is omitted while a drain line is shown, for a stale snapshot, and for daemons predating the `coordinator_connection` state field.

Security-relevant reading: the line is a local read-only diagnostic and does not itself grant serving authorization. This is consistent with the TB-011 and T-052 posture that diagnostics and labels are not authorization. It adds no endpoint, no new data egress and no change to key custody or the T-041 prefix-cache design. The text exposes no tokens, account identifiers or prompt content. The reason strings listed are generic: locked keychain, stalled Apple call, App Attest unavailable, no linked account.

Open integration question for a later pass: if StatusCommand+Traffic.swift derives 'eligible' from a cached local snapshot, it could overstate current authorization when the lease or revocation state changed. The doc mitigates this by omitting the line for stale snapshots and covering the expired-lease case. The code is not in this batch, so I cannot verify it. I have no evidence of a regression, so I raise no finding. The remainder of the file, including the logout, revoke, drain and autopilot text, is unchanged context and I did not evaluate it as new behavior.
